parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation; anti-discrimination law covers goods/services and a 2013 hate-crime statute covers gender identity — visitor-facing protections on paper, with documented but uneven operation (mediated film complaints, one ruling in favour; slow, bureaucratically impeded investigations). No facility bans, police campaigns or organised targeting are documented; borders, custody and LGR are open questions, which weigh lightly. Negatives: majority-conservative social attitudes with recent polling showing low acceptance (though mostly about homosexuality, not trans identity), 2016 constitutional removal of SO/GI protections under faith-based pressure, and ten logged anti-trans violence cases in a year that cannot be benchmarked against a background rate — real but unquantified. The profile resembles the elevated tier (uneven remedies, social hostility) rather than documented-acceptance jurisdictions, but formal protections and partial functioning keep it at its upper edge: 0.58.
